title: Gender data is becoming policy infrastructure for care, safety, climate, governance, and economic agency
source_unit: UN Women, Women Count Final Phase II Annual Report: Women Count: A Proven Pathway for Change
geography: Global gender-statistics systems, with Phase II country and regional support across Bangladesh, Cameroon, Colombia, Kenya, Morocco, Senegal, Tanzania, Uganda, and six regions

observations.period: 2019-2026; SDG 5 data availability and measurement gap

denominator.unit: Sustainable Development Goals and associated gender-equality monitoring system

sdg5_status.value: none of the SDG 5 indicators had been fully met; one was close to target, 10 were within reach at a moderate distance, and three were far or very far

data_financing_share.unit: percent of total statistics funding allocated to gender data in 2023

measurement_gap.value: four SDG 5 indicators lacked sufficient data for reliable monitoring

observations.method: UN Women synthesis using SDG data archives, gender-statistics system assessments, programme monitoring, and national and regional implementation evidence.
observations.uncertainty: Indicator availability and target status depend on definitions, revisions, reporting cycles, and whether data exist at the required frequency and disaggregation; data availability is not outcome progress.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, national statistical offices, ministries, civil society, policymakers, and groups whose experiences are missing from official statistics.
observations.counterinterpretation: Improved data can reveal problems rather than immediately solve them; policy, financing, political will, safety, and institutional capacity remain necessary for change.

observations.period: 2022-2025; scale and institutional reach of Women Count Phase II

country_support.unit: countries supported to strengthen gender-data systems, production, policy uptake, or innovative data use

trained_users.unit: data producers and users whose skills were strengthened through training

observations.method: UN Women programme monitoring and final Phase II reporting across national, regional, and global partnerships.
observations.uncertainty: Programme reach and training counts do not establish sustained institutional capacity, equal participation, data quality, or causal policy improvement in every supported country.
observations.subgroup: Statisticians, policymakers, gender ministries, civil society, researchers, data users, and women and girls represented by gender-data systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Coordination structures can improve continuity and accountability but may also add administrative layers or remain weak if domestic financing and political ownership decline.

denominator.unit: Women Count Phase II data-production portfolio

observations.method: UN Women programme reporting on gender data production for unpaid care, violence against women, climate and disasters, and environmental policy.
observations.uncertainty: Survey support and new standards improve measurement capacity but do not by themselves reveal prevalence in all populations, eliminate violence, or change care burdens and climate exposure.
observations.subgroup: Women and girls, unpaid caregivers, survivors, people exposed to climate and disaster risks, migrants, and persons with disabilities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Specialized surveys can improve visibility but may increase respondent burden, omit hard-to-reach groups, or fail to translate into budgets, services, protection, or accountability.

denominator.unit: Women Count policy-use and institutional uptake frame

policies_informed.unit: countries where policies or laws were informed by gender data

national_plans_informed.unit: countries using gender data to inform or update national development, gender-equality, social-protection, or other plans and policies

data_to_action_route.value: gender data were used in policy, planning, budgeting, legal reform, survivor services, disaster-risk reduction, and national climate contributions in reported examples

observations.method: UN Women final-report synthesis of policy uptake, country stories, gender-responsive budgeting, national planning, and data-user/data-producer dialogue.
observations.uncertainty: Being informed by data does not establish that data caused a policy change, that implementation followed, or that outcomes were equitable or durable.
observations.subgroup: Women’s organizations, government planners, budget officials, local authorities, service providers, survivors, caregivers, and communities affected by climate or conflict.
observations.counterinterpretation: Policy uptake can be selective or symbolic; data may be available and cited while resource allocation, enforcement, and lived conditions remain unchanged.

related_sources.claim: UN Women Data Hub landing page provides publication metadata, regional briefs, and programme overview.
UN Women Gender Snapshot provides complementary global gender-equality and SDG progress context.

boundary: This record adds a gender-data-to-policy route linking measurement, unpaid care, violence, environment, governance, crisis response, national statistical capacity, and accountability. It is a programme and aggregate policy-evidence synthesis, not respondent-level gender histories, prevalence estimates for every population, or proof that data-informed policy produces equal outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official UN Women Women Count Phase II final annual report and Data Hub page were reviewed for SDG 5 data gaps, programme reach, coordination, training, time-use, violence, gender-environment, and policy-uptake claims.
